description: Repo-scale (terraform-webapp): a new scale-in autoscaling policy + low-cpu alarm must maintain a real hysteresis gap below the existing high-cpu alarm's threshold - not just be numerically lower
prompts: Add `aws_autoscaling_policy.scale_in` in asg.tf (adjustment_type `ChangeInCapacity`, scaling_adjustment `-1`, cooldown `300`) referencing `aws_autoscaling_group.app.name`. Add a new `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.low_cpu` in cloudwatch.tf (comparison_operator `LessThanThreshold`, same metric/namespace/period/statistic/evaluation_periods as the existing `high_cpu` alarm, dimensions referencing `aws_autoscaling_group.app.name` the same way `high_cpu` does) that triggers the scale-in policy via `alarm_actions = [aws_autoscaling_policy.scale_in.arn]`. Critically, the low_cpu alarm's `threshold` must maintain a REAL hysteresis gap below `high_cpu`'s existing threshold of 80 - at least 20 percentage points lower (60 or below), not just numerically less than 80. A threshold too close to 80 (like 75) risks the scale-out and scale-in alarms flapping back and forth near the same utilization level.

test_setup_files.check_hysteresis_gap.py:
import json
import re
import subprocess

init = subprocess.run(['terraform', 'init', '-backend=false', '-input=false'],
                      capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
assert init.returncode == 0, f'terraform init failed:\n{init.stdout}\n{init.stderr}'

validate = subprocess.run(['terraform', 'validate', '-no-color', '-json'], capture_output=True, text=True)
data = json.loads(validate.stdout)
assert data.get('valid') is True, f'terraform validate failed: {validate.stdout}\n{validate.stderr}'

asg = open('asg.tf', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert 'aws_autoscaling_policy' in asg and 'scale_in' in asg, 'aws_autoscaling_policy.scale_in not found'
assert re.search(r'autoscaling_group_name\s*=\s*aws_autoscaling_group\.app\.name', asg), (
    'the scale-in policy must reference aws_autoscaling_group.app.name')

cw = open('cloudwatch.tf', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert 'aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "low_cpu"' in cw, 'aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.low_cpu not found'
assert re.search(r'alarm_actions\s*=\s*\[aws_autoscaling_policy\.scale_in\.arn\]', cw), (
    'low_cpu alarm must trigger the scale_in policy via alarm_actions')

low_block_match = re.search(r'resource\s+"aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm"\s+"low_cpu"\s*\{(.*?)\n\}', cw, re.DOTALL)
assert low_block_match, 'could not parse the low_cpu alarm block'
low_block = low_block_match.group(1)
m = re.search(r'threshold\s*=\s*(\d+)', low_block)
assert m, 'low_cpu alarm is missing a threshold'
low_threshold = int(m.group(1))

assert low_threshold <= 60, (
    f'low_cpu threshold ({low_threshold}) does not leave a real hysteresis gap below the existing '
    f'high_cpu threshold (80) - it must be at least 20 points lower (60 or below), otherwise the '
    f'scale-out and scale-in alarms can flap back and forth near the same utilization level')

print('PASS')

reference_solution.cloudwatch.tf:
resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "high_cpu" {
  alarm_name          = "webapp-high-cpu"
  comparison_operator = "GreaterThanThreshold"
  evaluation_periods  = 3
  metric_name         = "CPUUtilization"
  namespace           = "AWS/EC2"
  period              = 60
  statistic           = "Average"
  threshold           = 80

  dimensions = {
    AutoScalingGroupName = aws_autoscaling_group.app.name
  }
}

resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "low_cpu" {
  alarm_name          = "webapp-low-cpu"
  comparison_operator = "LessThanThreshold"
  evaluation_periods  = 3
  metric_name         = "CPUUtilization"
  namespace           = "AWS/EC2"
  period              = 60
  statistic           = "Average"
  threshold           = 60
  alarm_actions       = [aws_autoscaling_policy.scale_in.arn]

  dimensions = {
    AutoScalingGroupName = aws_autoscaling_group.app.name
  }
}
